subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Levels 0 to 2: Human in Charge
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Levels 0 to 2: Human in Charge.

hook.text: The SAE defined six levels of driving automation, from zero to five—most cars today sit at level two.

buildup.text: Level 0 means no automation at all—the driver does everything. Level 1 adds cruise control or lane assist.

discovery.text: Level 2 lets the car steer and brake at the same time, but the driver must watch the road constantly.

twist.text: Many drivers treat Level 2 like full self-driving, taking their hands off the wheel entirely.

climax.text: This dangerous gap between what Level 2 can do and what drivers think it can do causes real crashes.

punchline.text: Level 2 helps you drive—it doesn't drive for you.

quiz.question: At Level 2 automation, who must watch the road?

details.summary: SAE Levels 0 through 2 describe vehicle automation where the human driver remains fully responsible, from no automation at Level 0 to combined steering-and-acceleration assist at Level 2.
details.whyItMatters: Most cars on the road today operate at Levels 0 to 2. Understanding these levels clarifies that features marketed as autopilot still require constant human attention and do not make a car self-driving.
takeaways: Level 0 has no automation, Level 1 has single-function assist
Level 2 combines steering and speed control but the driver must watch
Tesla Autopilot and GM Super Cruise are Level 2 systems

faq.question: Is Tesla's Full Self-Driving actually Level 2?
faq.answer: Yes. Despite its name, Tesla's Full Self-Driving Supervised is classified as Level 2. The driver must remain attentive and ready to take over at all times. The marketing name has drawn criticism from safety advocates.

faq.question: What is the difference between Level 1 and Level 2?
faq.answer: Level 1 assists with either steering or speed control, like adaptive cruise control or lane keeping. Level 2 handles both simultaneously, but the driver must still monitor the road and be ready to intervene.
